facts.text: The study used a closed-loop high-throughput campaign combining automated synthesis, post-ageing activity screening, machine-learning prediction, Bayesian optimisation, and inverse analysis to select catalyst compositions and synthesis settings.
The campaign synthesised 1548 catalysts and evaluated 1493 of them.
Elemental composition and continuous-solvothermal synthesis parameters spanning 200–350 °C and 20–35 MPa were iteratively selected using post-ageing catalytic activity as the main design index.
Catalysts were thermally aged at 900 °C for 5 h under cyclic lean/rich, water-containing gas before activity testing.
After oxidation and reduction at 500 °C, catalytic light-off was measured from 100 to 500 °C at a ramp rate of 10 °C min−1 and a total gas flow of 500 mL min−1.
Beneficial ageing-induced electronic reconstruction produced coupled Cu–Pt adsorption sites that weakened overly strong CO binding and improved redox buffering and oxygen mobility.

High alkalinity and moderately low synthesis temperature promoted synchronous multimetal reduction while limiting detrimental segregation and incorporation of Fe, Ni, or Cu into La–Al-based mixed oxides.
During reaction, i-C5H12 oxidation depleted oxygen and generated locally reduced sites that enabled NO reduction.
Inverse-model-guided exploration produced substantially higher post-ageing hit rates than random exploration for T50, conversion at 350 °C, and integrated conversion.
Predictive exploration achieved hit rates of 27.0%, 44.3%, and 37.2% for T50, 350 °C conversion, and overall conversion, respectively, versus 1.3%, 3.1%, and 1.5% for random exploration.

For matched compositions, high-alkali synthesis at 245 °C increased 350 °C conversion by 64, 21, 28, and 73 percentage points for NO, CO, C3H6, and i-C5H12, respectively, relative to lower-alkali synthesis at 264 °C.
After ageing, catalyst hts0025 increased NO and i-C5H12 conversion at 350 °C by 52% and 75% and lowered their T50 values by 134 °C and 124 °C, respectively.
